5001.lxx: in LXX for כָּסָה pi., שָׁבַץ pu., etc.
5001.full: περι-καλύπτω [in LXX for כָּסָה pi., שָׁבַץ pu., etc. ;] to cover around, cover up or over. with accusative, Mrk.14:65, Luk.22:64; pass., before χρυσίῳ, Heb.9:4.† (AS)

s: to be built up, walled in
the space built round, the enclosure
5002.full: 1. to build round , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to enclose by building round , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be built up, walled in , (Thucydides); τὸ περιοικοδομημένον the space built round, the enclosure , Lat. ovile, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

5003.full: περι-ποίησις, -εως, ἡ (περιποιέω), [in LXX: 2Ch.4:13 (12) (מִחְיָה) Mal.3:17 (סְגֻלָּה), Hag.2:10 (9) * ;] __1. preservation: Heb.10:39 (2 Ch, l.with). __2. acquisition, obtaining: 1Th.5:9, 2Th.2:14 (and so perh. Eph.1:14, see infr.). __3. a possession: Eph.1:14 (but see supr., and cf. ICC, in l), 1Pe.2:9 (LXX).† (AS)

s: to be turned round, spin round
5004.full: 1. to whirl round , of one preparing to throw, (Homer); π. ἵππον to wheel it round , (Plutarch):—; Pass. to be turned round, spin round , (Iliad by Homer); π. εἰς τἀληθῆ to come round to it, (Plato Philosophus) 2. π. τὼ χεῖρε to tie his hands behind him, (Lysias Orator). (ML)

5005.full: 1. to drag about , ἄνω καὶ κάτω (Lucian) 2. to tear away from , τί τινος (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

5006.full: περι-φρονέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 4Ma.6:9 4Mac 14:1 * ;] __1. to examine on all sides, consider carefully (Aristoph.). __2. = ὑπερφρονέω, to have thouphts beyond, to despise (Thuc., Plut., al.; 4Mac, ll. with) : Tit.2:15.† (AS)

5007.full: περι-φέρω [in LXX: Ecc.7:8 (7) (הָלַל po.), al. ;] to carry about: Mrk.6:55, 2Co.4:10. Pass., metaphorically: Eph.4:14.† (AS)

5008.full: exceeding joyous or glad , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τινι at a thing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; τὸ π. excessive joy , (Thucydides) (ML)

s: to have around one, be clothed with
5011.full: περί-κειμαι [in LXX: Ep. Je 24, 58, 4Ma.12:3 * ;] __1. to lie round about: μύλος, λίθος (RV, were hanged about), Mrk.9:42, Luk.17:2; νεφος μαρτύρων, Heb.12:1. __2. to have around one, be clothed with: Act.28:20; figuratively, ἀσθένειαν, Heb.5:2.† (AS)

5014.full: 1. to leap, spring, bound , ὑψόσε ποσσὶν ἐπήδα (Iliad by Homer); π. ἐς σκάφος (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative cognate, πήδημα πηδᾶν to take a leap, (Euripides); with accusative loci, πεδία πηδᾶν to bound over them, (Sophocles Tragicus); π. πλάκα (Euripides) 2. metaphorically of an arrow, (Iliad by Homer); of the heart, to leap, throb , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; of sudden changes, τί πηδᾶις εἰς ἄλλους τρόπου; (Euripides) (ML)

5015.full: πηλίκος, -η, -ον [in LXX: Zec.2:2 (6) (כָּמַהּ), 4Ma.15:22 * ;] interrog., how large, how great ? (prop., of magnitude, as πόσος of quantity): in exclamations, = ἡλίκος (see Bl., § 51, 4), Gal.6:11; of personal greatness, Heb.7:4.† (AS)

5017.lxx: in LXX: Hab.2:9, Eze.22:27 (בָּצַע), Jdg.4:11 B*
5017.full: πλεονεκτέω, -ῶ (πλεονέκτης, which see), [in LXX: Hab.2:9, Eze.22:27 (בָּצַע), Jdg.4:11 B* ;] __1. intrans., to have more, to have an advantage (cl., with genitive of person(s)). __2. Trans., in late writers (see M, Pr., 65), to over­reach, defraud: with accusative of person(s), 2Co.7:2 12:17-18; ἐν τ. πράγματιι, 1Th.4:6 (see M, Th., in l); pass., 2Co.2:11 (as also in cl.; see LS, see word).† (AS)

5018.full: 1. to be or become full , τινός of a thing, (Euripides):—; absolute, ἀγορῆς πληθυούσης, see. ἀγορά V.:—;of rivers, to swell, rise , (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid., (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to increase in number, multiply , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. to abound , τινί in a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to be general, prevail , Lat. invalescere, of reports, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὁ πληθύων χρόνος increasing time, age, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

5027.full: 1. much-tangled, thick-wreathed , of a serpent's coils, (Euripides); of the polypus, with tangled, twisting arms , (Theognis Elegiacus) 2. metaphorically much-twisting, complex, intricate , [Refs 5th c.BC, 5th/4th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

5029.full: 1. a broidered stuff, brocade , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. broidered work, broidery , (Homer) 3. generally, a variety, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

5031.full: προβατικός, -ή, -όν (πρόβατον) [in LXX (π. πύλη): Neh.3:1, 32 12:39 (צֹאן)* ;] of sheep: ἡ π. (sc. πύλη, see supr.), the sheep-gate, Jhn.5:2.† (AS)

5032.full: προ-γινώσκω [in LXX: Wis.6:13 8:8 18:6 * ;] to know beforehand, foreknow: 2Pe.3:17; with accusative of person(s), Act.26:5; of the Divine foreknowledge, Rom.8:29 11:2, 1Pe.1:20.† (AS)

5033.full: προ-δίδωμι [in LXX: Eze.16:34 A (נָתַן), 4Ma.4:1, al. ;] __1. to give before, give first: Rom.11:35 (Job.41:2 (11) LXX, al.). __2. to betray (4Mac, l.with).† (AS)

5034.full: 1. an opening or introduction to a thing; in Music, a prelude, overture , (Pindar); in poems and speeches, a proem, preface, preamble, introduction , Lat. exordium, (Pindar) 2. metaphorically of any prelude or beginning , φροίμιον χορεύσομαι (Aeschulus Tragicus); μηδέπω ' ν προοιμίοις only just beginning , (Aeschulus Tragicus); εἴ τι τοῦδε φρ. ματᾷ if any part of this presage be vain, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. generally, a hymn , (Thucydides) (ML)

5035.full: προπετής, -ές (προπίπτω), [in LXX: Pro.10:14 (אֱוִיל) Pro.13:3 (פָּשַׂק) Sir.9:18 * ;] falling forwards, headlong. Metaphorical, precipitate, rash, reck­less: of persons, 2Ti.3:4; of things, Act.19:36.† (AS)

5036.lxx: in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ, also for עָבַר, etc.
5036.full: προ-πορεύω [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ, also for עָבַר, etc. ;] to make to go before. Pass. and mid., to go before: Luk.1:76, Act.7:40" (LXX) ,† (AS)

5038.full: 1. to look laughing at one, τινά (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; with accusative cognate, προσγελᾶτε τὸν πανύστατον γέλων smile your last smile upon me, (Euripides) 2. metaphorically, like Lat. arrideo, to delight, ὀσμὴ βροτείων αἱμάτων με προσγελᾷ (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

5040.full: προσ-κεφάλαιον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Eze.13:18, 20 (כֶּסֶת), I Est.3:8 * ;] a pillow, cushion: Mrk.4:38.† (AS)

s: to take offence at, be angry with
5041.full: 1. to strike against , τινί (Plato Philosophus):absolute to stumble, fail , (Plutarch) 2. to have a collision with another, give offence , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. τινί (Plutarch) 3. to take offence at, be angry with , τινί (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: —;absolute to take offence , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

5042.lxx: in LXX: 1Ki.21:13 (14) (הָלַל hithpo.), Job.19:14, (Sir 34:30 (Sir.31:30)), Dan LXX Su 1:11 *
5042.full: προσ-ποιέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 1Ki.21:13 (14) (הָלַל hithpo.), Job.19:14, (Sir 34:30 (Sir.31:30)), Dan LXX Su 1:11 * ;] to make over to, add or attach to. Mid., to take to oneself, claim; hence, to pretend; with inf. (cf. Xen., Anab., iv, 3, 20), to make as if: Luk.24:28.† (AS)

5043.full: προσφιλής, -ές (φιλέω), [in LXX: Est.5:1, Sir.4:7 20:13 * ;] __(a) of persons, in both act, and pass. sense (LXX, ll. with); __(b) of things, pleas­ing, agreeable (EV, lovely): Php.4:8.† (AS)

s: to run on, run in advance
5045.lxx: in LXX: 1Ki.8:11 (פָּנִים רוּץ), Job.41:13 (14) A (דּוּץ), Tob.11:3 (before ἔμπροσθεν), 1Ma.16:21 *
5045.full: προ-τρέχω [in LXX: 1Ki.8:11 (פָּנִים רוּץ), Job.41:13 (14) A (דּוּץ), Tob.11:3 (before ἔμπροσθεν), 1Ma.16:21 * ;] __1. to run forward. __2. to run on, run in advance: Jhn.20:4; before εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν, Luk.19:4.† (AS)

s: excuse, allege by way of excuse, plead in excuse
to allege as an excuse that
to be used as a pretext
5046.full: 1. Dep.: 2. to set up as a pretext or excuse, allege by way of excuse, plead in excuse , with accusative, (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; with infinitive to allege as an excuse that . . , (Demosthenes Orator):—;absolute to make excuses , (Thucydides):—;aor1 προφασισθῆναι in passive sense, to be used as a pretext , (Thucydides) 3. to allege (by way of accusation) that , (Plato Philosophus) from πρόφᾶσις (ML)

s: to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place
5047.full: πρωτεύω (πρῶτος) [in LXX: Est.5:11, 2Ma.6:18 2Mac 13:15 * ;] to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place: Col.1:18.† (AS)

5050.full: πρό-δηλος, -ον [in LXX: Jdth.8:29, 2Ma.3:17 2Mac 14:39 * ;] __1. evident beforehand. __2. clearly evident: 1Ti.5:24-25 Heb.7:14.† (AS)

5051.full: πρό-δρομος, -ον (προτρέχω) [in LXX: Num.13:21 (20), Isa.28:4 (בִּכּוּר), Wis.12:8 * ;] running forward, going in advance. As subst., ὁ π., an advance guard, forerunner: Heb.6:20.† (AS)

5052.full: a deposit made by water , πρ. Νείλου, of the Delta of the Nile, (Aeschulus Tragicus) from προσχώννυ_μι (ML)

5053.full: 1. to make close, cover or wrap up, enwrap , (Iliad by Homer); π. νῆα λίθοισι to surround a ship with stones, so as to protect it when laid up, (Hesiod):—; to cover thickly , of a youth's chin, (Odyssey by Homer); πυκ. στεφάνοις to cover thick with crowns, (Euripides); so in Mid., στεφάνοις κεφαλὰς πυκασώμεθα [variant datesAnthology Palantina; also without στεφάνοις, to crown, deck with garlands , (Euripides):—;Pass., στέμμασι πυκασθείς (Herdotus Historicus); δάφνῃ πυκασθείς (Euripides); perfect participle πεπυκασμένος, thickly covered , ὄρος πεπυκασμένον a hill well-clothed with wood, (Hesiod):—;Mid., πυκάζου cover thyself , (Euripides) 2. metaphorically, Ἕκτορα ἄχος πύκασε φρένας threw a shadow over his heart, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., νόον πεπυκασμένος, close, cautious of mind, (Hesiod) 3. to close, shut, shut up , ἐντὸς πυκάζειν σφέας αὐτούς to shut themselves close up within, (Odyssey by Homer); πύκαζε (i.e. τὸ δῶμα); shut it close , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

s: anything made of it, linen, cord
5056.full: 1. the papyrus , an Egyptian rush with triangular stalks: paper was made by peeling off its outer coat βύβλος); and gluing the slips together. 2. anything made of it, linen, cord , etc., [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

5057.full: πἡρα, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Jdth.10:5 13:10, 15 * ;] a leathern pouch for victuals, etc., a wallet (Deiss. thinks an alms-bag, see LAE, 108 ff.): Mat.10:10, Mrk.6:8, Luk.9:3 10:4 22:35-36.† (AS)

5058.full: πίμπρημι (in cl. prose, rare in the simple form), [in LXX: Num.5:21-22, 27 (צָבֶה) * ;] __1. to blow, burn. __2. Later, to cause to swell; mid., of parts of the body, to become swollen (LXX) : Act.28:6 (cf. ἐμπίπρημι).† (AS)

5059.full: the pine, stone pine , (Homer):—;proverbial, πίτυος τρόπον ἐκτρίβεσθαι to be destroyed like a pine , i. e. utterly , because the pine when cut down never grows again, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to be made to stumble, to stumble
5066.lxx: in LXX: Dan LXX 11:41 (כָּשַׁל ni.), Sir.9:5 (Sir.35:15 32:15) (יָקֹשׁ ho.) Sir.23:8 (also in Aq., Sm., Th., and in Psa Sol Psa.16:7; not elsewhere, except NT and eccl.)*
5066.full: σκανδαλίζω (σκάνδαλον), [in LXX: Dan LXX 11:41 (כָּשַׁל ni.), Sir.9:5 (Sir.35:15 32:15) (יָקֹשׁ ho.) Sir.23:8 (also in Aq., Sm., Th., and in Psa Sol Psa.16:7; not elsewhere, except NT and eccl.)* ;] prop., to put a snare or stumbling-block in the way; in NT always metaphorically of that which hinders right conduct or thought, to cause to stumble: with accusative of person(s), Mat.5:29-30 17:27 18:6, 8-9 Mrk.9:42-43, 45 9:47 Luk.17:2, Jhn.6:61, 1Co.8:13. Pass., to be made to stumble, to stumble: Mat.11:6 13:21, 57 15:12 24:10 26:31, 33, Mrk.4:17 6:3 14:27, 29, Luk.7:23, Jhn.16:1, Rom.14:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), 2Co.11:29,† (AS)

5067.lxx: in LXX: Deu.10:16, Jer.4:4 (לֵבָב עׇרְלָה), Sir.16:10 (cf. καρδία σκληρά, Sir.3:26-27) *
5067.full: σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ (σκληρός, καρδία), [in LXX: Deu.10:16, Jer.4:4 (לֵבָב עׇרְלָה), Sir.16:10 (cf. καρδία σκληρά, Sir.3:26-27) * ;] hardness of heart: Mat.19:8, Mrk.10:5 16:14.† (AS)

5069.full: ακοπέω, -ῶ (σκοπός), [in LXX: Est.8:13, 2Ma.4:5 * ;] to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaphorical, to look to, consider: with accusative of thing(s), 2Co.4:13, Php.2:4; with accusative of person(s), Rom.16:17, Php.3:17; before μή, Luk.11:35; σεαυτόν, before μή (see M, Pr., 192), Gal.6:1 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).† SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω (AS)

5070.full: σκοτία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Job.28:3 (אֹפֶל), Mic.3:6 (חָשַׁךְ), Isa.16:3 * ;] in late writers = σκότος, darkness: Jhn.6:17 20:1. Metaphorical, __(a) of secrecy (opposite to ἐν τ. φωτί): Mat.10:27, Luk.12:3; __(b) of spiritual darkness: Mat.4:16, Jhn.1:5 8:12 12:35, 40, 1Jn.1:5 Jn 2:8-9 Jn 2:11.† (AS)

5072.lxx: in LXX: Dan LXX Bel 1:32, TH Bel 1:33 *
5072.full: σκάφη, -ης, ἡ (σκάπτω), [in LXX: Dan LXX Bel 1:32, TH Bel 1:33 * ;] anything scooped out, esp. a light boat, skiff: Act.27:16, 30 27:32.† (AS)

s: to look to, view, examine, consider, think on
5073.full: 1. to look about, look carefully , followed by preposition εἰς, (Odyssey by Homer):—;with accusative to look after, watch , (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;absolute to look out, reconnoitre , (Herdotus Historicus); σκέψαι look , (Aeschulus Tragicus); σκέψασθε look out , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of the mind, to look to, view, examine, consider, think on , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—; σκέψασθε δέ: only consider , (Thucydides) 3. to think of beforehand, premeditate , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. perfect also in passive sense, ἐσκεμμένα things well-considered , (Thucydides); σκοπεῖτε οὖν. Answ. ἔσκεπται (Plato Philosophus); so 3 future passive ἐσκέψεται (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

5074.g: a feeding on the inwards of a sacrifice
5074.full: a feeding on the inwards of a sacrifice

5076.lxx: in LXX: Gen.1:29, Lev.11:37 (זָרַע), Sir 40:22 א1 *
5076.full: σπόριμος, -ον (σπείρω) [in LXX: Gen.1:29, Lev.11:37 (זָרַע), Sir 40:22 א1 * ;] fit for sowing, sown; as subst., τὰ σ., corn-fields: Mat.12:1, Mrk.2:23, Luk.6:1.† (AS)

5079.full: 1. round, spherical , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λίθοι στρ. pebbles , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. circular , (Plato Philosophus) 3. round, compactly formed , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. of ships, στρ. ναῦς, στρ. πλοῖον, a merchant- ship, from its round shape , as opposite to the long narrow ship-of-war μακρὰ ναῦς); (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 5. metaphorically of phrases, well-rounded, compact, pithy, terse , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;adverb, στρογγυλώτατα as tersely as possible , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

s: as they danced from right to left of the
the strain sung during this evolution, the strophe
5080.full: 1. a turning , e.g. of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν στροφαῖσιν ὀμμάτων with rolling of the eyes, (Euripides) 2. a twist , such as wrestlers make to elude their adversary, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically a trick, dodge , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. the turning of the Chorus as they danced from right to left of the ὀρχήστρα: the strain sung during this evolution, the strophe , to which the ἀντιστροφή answers. (ML)

5081.lxx: in LXX: Psa.49:17 (יָרַד), Wis.10:13, Dan LXX TH 3:49 *
5081.full: συν-κατα-βαίνω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psa.49:17 (יָרַד), Wis.10:13, Dan LXX TH 3:49 * ;] to go down with: Act.25:5. In late writers also metaphorically (Wis, l.with), to condescend, on WH. see Rutherford, NPhr., 485 f.† (AS)

s: to deposit one's vote with, hence, to agree with, assent to
5082.lxx: in LXX: Exo.23:1 (שִׁית יָד), Exo.23:32 (בְּרִית), Da TH Su 1:20 *
5082.full: συν-κατα-τίθημι (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Exo.23:1 (שִׁית יָד), Exo.23:32 (בְּרִית), Da TH Su 1:20 * ;] to deposit together. Mid., to deposit one's vote with, hence, to agree with, assent to: with dative, Luk.23:51.† (AS)

5085.full: συν-κάμπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psa.68:10, 23 (מעד hi.), etc. ;] to bend completely, bend together: τ. νῶτον, figuratively, Rom.11:10 (LXX).† (AS)

5086.full: συν-κύπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job.9:27 (עָזַב), Sir.12:11 19:26 * ;] __1. to bend forwards (Arist., al.). __2. to be bowed down: Luk.13:11.† (AS)

5088.g: to rest under the same roof.
s: to help to solve a difficulty
to rest under the same roof
5088.full: 1. to help in loosing , (Euripides):—; to help to solve a difficulty or end a quarrel , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to rest under the same roof , (Aeschulus Tragicus); compare καταλύω. (ML)

5090.lxx: in LXX: Gen.19:17 (סָפָה ni.), Job.1:4 (שָׁלַח ni), 3Ma.1:1 *
5090.full: συν-παρα-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Gen.19:17 (סָפָה ni.), Job.1:4 (שָׁלַח ni), 3Ma.1:1 * ;] to take along with: as a companion, with accusative, Act.12:25 15:37-38 (on the tenses, see M, Pr., 130), Gal.2:1.† (AS)

5092.full: to knead together: beat black and blue , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;Pass., (Euripides); ψυχὴ συμπέφυρται μετὰ τοῦ κακοῦ (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

5094.full: 1. to turn back together , intransitive, (Plutarch) 2. Pass. and Mid. to live along with or among others, with dative, (Plutarch) (ML)

5097.full: συν-απο-στέλλω [in LXX: Exo.33:2, 12 (שָׁלַח), I Est.5:2 * ;] to send along with: with accusative, 2Co.12:18 (cf. MM, xxiv).† (AS)
